clarity_findings.claim: The worked example under "How they combine" jumps straight into an indented block of made-up numbers (production 150, 12 workforce, 15 mobilized...) with no signal that these are an illustrative scenario rather than real game constants.
clarity_findings.problem: Every number in the block is a plain literal with no {const:}/{rate:} token and no lead-in like mobility.md's "Example (Legacy):", so a reader can momentarily read 150/12/15/20%/25%/−50 as actual baseline values instead of an invented walkthrough.
clarity_findings.fix: Add a short lead-in such as "Example:" before the indented block, matching the pattern used on mobility.md, so the numbers are clearly framed as illustrative.

clarity_findings.claim: The table's "Size" column promises a magnitude for each penalty but only the Besieged row actually states one ("all of its production"); the other two rows just point elsewhere ("see workforce", "set by the status").
clarity_findings.problem: A reader scanning the column header expects a comparable answer in every row, then finds two rows defer instead of answering, which reads as an inconsistent column contract even though deferring is correct under the guide map's ownership split.
clarity_findings.fix: Consider a header phrasing that sets the expectation correctly, e.g. "Size" -> "How much" or add a one-word qualifier so two deferred rows do not read as an unfulfilled promise.

clarity_findings.claim: The worked example under "How they combine" re-derives the workforce over-mobilization formula that the guide map assigns exclusively to the workforce page, instead of just citing the resulting percentage.
clarity_findings.problem: Line 49 reads "production 150, 12 workforce, 15 mobilized (1 − 12 ÷ 15 = 20 %):  150 − 20 % = 120". This restates, with the same numbers, the exact formula workforce.md already owns and shows ("12 workforce, 15 mobilized: outputs reduced by 20 %", "penalty = 1 − workforce ÷ mobilized"). The guide map's owner table gives "Workforce, over-mobilization" to `workforce` (existing), and the table row just above this example already does it right ("the share over-mobilized, see [[workforce]]"). Re-deriving the formula here violates rule 4 ("Point instead of half-explaining": link instead of a clause that summarizes the other page's mechanic) and duplicates a topic the guide map gives to another page beyond one sentence.
clarity_findings.fix: Take the 20 % as a given and link to workforce instead of re-deriving it, e.g. "production 150 with a 20 % workforce penalty (see [[workforce]]):  150 − 20 % = 120", dropping "12 workforce, 15 mobilized (1 − 12 ÷ 15 = 20 %)".

clarity_findings.claim: The final bullet under "What they reduce" crowds four items into one line while every other item gets its own bullet.
clarity_findings.problem: "{name:...sys_fighter_lvl}, {name:...sys_corvette_lvl}, {name:...sys_frigate_lvl} and {name:...sys_capital_lvl}" compiles to one bullet reading "Fighter Ships' Initial XP, Corvette Ships' Initial XP, Frigate Ships' Initial XP and Capital Ships' Initial XP", breaking the one-item-per-bullet rhythm of the six bullets above it and making the last line the hardest to scan.
clarity_findings.fix: Give each ship class its own bullet, or add a one-line lead-in ("Ships' Initial XP, for every class:") before four short bullets.

clarity_findings.claim: The worked example jumps from a production chain to an unrelated credit figure with no transition.
clarity_findings.problem: The first three lines of the example chain the same production value (150 → 120 → 90 → 0); the fourth line, "credit −50 in Protests:  stays −50", starts a separate scenario about a different output, but nothing marks the switch, so a reader may expect it to connect to the production number.
clarity_findings.fix: Add a short lead-in before the fourth line, e.g. "Separately, an output that starts negative stays untouched:", so it reads as its own case.

clarity_findings.claim: "There are three." is a clipped two-word sentence that reads as an afterthought right before the table.
clarity_findings.problem: Rule 1 asks for friendly, natural sentences; this fragment right after the definitional first sentence feels like a leftover count rather than a lead-in to the table that follows.
clarity_findings.fix: Fold it into the first sentence or rephrase as a lead-in, e.g. "There are three penalties:" directly before the table.
